story_type: Katrina rooftop hoist, man and boy pulled out through a roof
hook: He climbed out through a hole in his roof. The water was below.
narration: He came up through a hole in his own roof, and a Navy rescuer grabbed hold.
This was New Orleans on September first, 2005, three days after Hurricane Katrina hit.
Helicopter crews flew low over the flooded city, searching for people stranded in their homes.
When floodwater rises, people climb into the attic. Some have to break through the roof to be seen from the air.
The rescuer rides the cable down, wraps a sling around one person, and the hoist lifts them both together.
[short pause] Then a young boy came up, held tight against the rescuer's chest.
outcome: The helicopter crews pulled them off the rooftops and flew them out of the flood to safety.
title: Pulled out through a hole in the roof
description:
Navy helicopter crews hoisted people off flooded rooftops in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Sept. 1, 2005, days after Hurricane Katrina.
